explanation: RAII is a fundamental C++ programming technique that tightly couples resource management with object lifetime.  It ensures resources (like memory, files, network connections, mutexes) are automatically acquired when an object is created and released when the object goes out of scope. This eliminates resource leaks and simplifies error handling by leveraging the destructor.  It's a cornerstone of C++'s exception safety and promotes more robust and maintainable code.
